title: Simsimiyya (five-string lyre)
summary: The simsimiyya is a five-string lyre of the Suez Canal and the Red Sea coast. Its body is a metal drum with a skin face and a ring of rivets, and two slim arms painted blue carry a crossbar with steel tuning pins. Its bright, ringing steel strings keep time for sailors’ dance songs.
howToPlay: Five steel strings run from the pins on the crossbar to the bridge, the lowest on the left. Each lane marks a place to pluck a string.
A bead slides down a string. Pluck the lane as it lands.
The tunes are quick and repeat, as in the dance songs of the port towns.
Take the first tune slowly, then try the quick one.
rules: The strings are tuned to a scale with one neutral, in-between third.
A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
Tunes count four beats to the bar and are quick.
heritageNote: Along the Suez Canal the simsimiyya is played with song and dance in the evening. Makers often build the body from a metal tin or drum, and the steel strings give it a bright, bell-like ring.
